name: Sanathan Textiles Ltd
title: Sanathan Textiles Ltd - 544314 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Sanathan Textiles Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 79.08% YoY to INR1,334.74 crores, but PAT fell to INR23.82 crores on Punjab depreciation and finance costs.
summary.overview: Standalone performance improved sequentially and YoY, with EBITDA up 35.52% YoY to INR94.93 crores, driven by Silvassa and better spreads. Consolidated EBITDA rose 55.38% YoY to INR108.08 crores, but depreciation (INR34.7 crores) and finance costs (INR38.6 crores) rose sharply as Punjab moved from capitalisation into the P&L. Management said demand was deferred in April-May on raw material price volatility, with conditions normalising from June. Management maintained FY27 consolidated EBITDA guidance of INR520-540 crores.

financial_highlights.change: +14.46% QoQ, +55.38% YoY; margin broadly flat QoQ (8.08%), down from 9.33% YoY
+10.4% QoQ (vs INR21.57 crores), down from INR40.43 crores YoY
+15.10% QoQ, +35.52% YoY; margin up 72 bps QoQ and 233 bps YoY

segments.name: Silvassa (standalone; polyester, cotton, technical textiles)
segments.commentary: Standalone EBITDA margin 11.67%; management cited FY26 EBITDA per ton of about INR11,000 at Silvassa on a consolidated basis across polyester, cotton and technical yarn. Sold about 54,000 tonnes in Q1.

segments.name: Punjab (polyester filament yarn)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue about INR550 crores and EBITDA about INR12 crores (per CFO, in response to analyst question). Sold about 46,000 tonnes; polymerisation capacity 700 TPD at about 80% utilisation. Target FY28 EBITDA of about INR30,000 per ton.

segments.name: Technical textiles (Silvassa)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue about INR33 crores at about 94% utilisation on the 9,000 TPA line. Installed capacity expansion to 18,000 TPA is being commissioned; management expects about 7,500 tonnes of incremental capacity this year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated EBITDA guidance maintained at about INR520-540 crores, against INR108.08 crores in Q1.
Punjab Phase 1 (700 TPD) utilisation targeted at 85-90% in Q2 and 95-96% in the following quarter.
Punjab Phase 2 (+200 TPD, to 900 TPD) to be fully commissioned in Q1 FY28; management said the FY28 timeline is intact.
Punjab targeted to deliver about INR30,000 EBITDA per ton next year (filament yarn, polyester only).
Management expects better demand from end-August through September 2026.
32 MW hybrid wind-solar captive power to be commissioned in phases, expected to reduce power costs.
capex_capacity: Silvassa technical textile capacity raised from 9,000 to 18,000 TPA after plant and machinery installation; commercial production expected shortly, to be announced later.
Proposed greenfield cotton yarn plant in Madhya Pradesh: about INR400 crores capex for 72,500 spindles, asset turn 0.8-0.85x, implying INR350-375 crores incremental revenue.
Punjab polymerisation at 700 TPD, Phase 2 adds 200 TPD to reach 900 TPD in Q1 FY28.
Punjab ramp-up on Phase 2 expected to take 1.5 to 2 quarters to reach full capacity after commissioning.
demand_pricing: Q1 demand was deferred in April-May as PTA, MEG and raw cotton prices spiked; management said the deferral was a reaction to price rather than consumption, with normalisation from June.
Management said spreads improved across all three verticals Q4 to Q1, but did not give segment-level spread figures.
Pass-through of higher raw material costs happened with a delay; industry price adjustments began towards quarter close.
Government temporarily waived the 11% customs duty on raw cotton imports from June 1, 2026.
Inventory: polyester 12-13 days at both sites vs normal 10-12 days; cotton finished inventory about 7 days; raw material about 8-10 days at quarter end.

Feedstock: Silvassa sources about 50-60% imported PTA and 40% domestic PTA (40% contracted, 60% short-term rolling contracts); Punjab sources PTA from IOCL Panipat. Talks with GAIL and IOCL Paradip for future domestic supply; no contracts finalised.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA per ton and scale needed for Punjab to reach an 11-12% margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management redirected to EBITDA per ton, targeting about INR30,000 per ton for Punjab next year; Silvassa was about INR11,000 per ton for FY26 (consolidated across polyester, cotton, technical yarn).

qa_highlights.question: Why the large EBITDA-per-ton gap between Punjab and Silvassa?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR30,000 target covers only polyester filament yarn at Punjab, while the Silvassa INR11,000 figure is a blend of polyester, cotton and technical yarn.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Punjab Phase 2 FY28 timeline intact, and how fast will it ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, on track; full commissioning in Q1 FY28 taking capacity to 900 TPD, with 1.5-2 quarters needed to reach full run-rate.

qa_highlights.question: How much capex and revenue for the proposed MP cotton yarn plant?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR400 crores for 72,500 cotton spindles, asset turn 0.8-0.85x, giving INR350-375 crores incremental revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 EBITDA guidance still valid after Q1 EBITDA of INR108 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, guidance maintained at INR520-540 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of PTA supply from GAIL and IOCL?
qa_highlights.answer: No contracts yet; talks ongoing, and the company expects a phased shift from imported to domestic PTA once these plants start production.

risks_watch: Raw cotton pricing and availability, flagged by management as a key monitorable for the coming season amid climate-related disruption; cotton duty waiver from June 1, 2026 is temporary.
Demand recovery timing: management expects better demand from end-August through September 2026, after April-May deferrals; watch whether Q2 volumes and price pass-through confirm this.

Punjab ramp-up: Phase 1 utilisation was about 80% in Q1, targeted at 85-90% in Q2 and 95-96% the quarter after; Phase 2 (+200 TPD to 900 TPD) ramp is expected to take 1.5-2 quarters after commissioning.
FY27 consolidated EBITDA guidance of INR520-540 crores requires about INR412-432 crores over Q2-Q4 against INR108.08 crores in Q1, implying a steep step-up.
Finance costs (INR38.6 crores) and depreciation (INR34.7 crores) now fully in P&L as Punjab is commissioned; consolidated PAT margin of 1.78% is highly sensitive to these charges.
PTA feedstock: Silvassa relies on about 50-60% imported PTA; no long-term contracts yet with GAIL or IOCL Paradip, and the transition to domestic supply is expected to be phased.
key_quotes: It was a quarter defined less by demand and more by price.
That difference is the entire story.
We are maintaining the guidance of EBITDA between about INR520 crores to INR540 crores.
The deferral of purchases we saw through April and May was a reaction to price, not to underlying consumption.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operations and the FY27 guidance, which was reiterated despite a weak consolidated PAT, but cautious on demand, saying the geopolitical environment remains fluid and the full impact is hard to assess. Management was evasive on segment-level spreads and on the timing of GAIL and IOCL PTA supply, declining to give figures or confirm contracts.

adds.what: Silvassa technical textile capacity expansion from 9,000 to 18,000 TPA (about 7,500 t incremental this year)
Punjab polymerisation Phase 2 adds 200 TPD (to 900 TPD)
Proposed greenfield cotton yarn plant in Madhya Pradesh, 72,500 spindles
32 MW hybrid wind-solar captive power (power cost reduction, not production capacity)

growth.why: Q1 consolidated revenue rose 79% YoY and management held FY27 EBITDA guidance at INR520-540 crore against INR108 crore in Q1, but Q1 demand was deferred on price volatility, and Punjab utilisation is only about 80%, so the growth case is solid but not yet proven.
